source_doubts.quote: the source concludes by the companion unitarizability theorem \cite[Theorem~1.1]{OpenAIUnitarizability2026}
source_doubts.problem: The whole proof is a citation to a companion theorem whose statement is not reproduced, in both source and rewrite. As invoked (hypotheses: countable and nonamenable; conclusion: a non-unitarizable representation with bound 1+epsilon), that theorem would settle Dixmier's unitarizability problem, which is open as far as I know. Neither the hypotheses nor the 1+epsilon bound can be checked from this document. The corollary is not used in the proof of Theorem 1.1.

source_doubts.quote: The source applies the companion percolation result \cite[Corollary~1.2]{OpenAIPercolation2026} to $F$, nonamenable by Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
source_doubts.problem: The whole proof is a citation to a companion result whose statement is not reproduced, in both source and rewrite. The conclusions (bounded T_{p_c}, p_c < p_{2->2} <= p_u for every finite symmetric generating set, infinitely many infinite clusters on (p_c,p_u), and the simultaneous statement on [p_1,p_2]) amount to the Benjamini–Schramm p_c < p_u conjecture for all Cayley graphs of a nonamenable group, which is open in general as far as I know. Nothing here can be checked from this document. The corollary is not used in the proof of Theorem 1.1.
